title: Thermal-aware autoscaler for on-prem dedicated pools — PRD draft
body:
Overview:
This doc proposes a thermal-aware autoscaling layer for Redwood Dedicated on-prem pools. Motivation: on-prem racks have thermal and power constraints that can force sudden throttling or GPU downclocking, which degrades latency and throughput and violates customer SLOs. Current autoscalers focus on utilization and queue depth; they ignore thermal dynamics (heat soak, HVAC lag, rack-level hotspots). The proposed feature augments the autoscaler with a predictive thermal model and burst-credit system to preserve SLOs while avoiding sustained thermal overload.

Goals:
- Keep per-tenant latency SLOs within targets under sustained and bursty load while respecting site thermal limits.
- Provide configurable safety bands for different datacenter classes (edge closet, co-lo, private data center).
- Offer transparent behavior: explainable throttling/fallback reasons in Console and runbooks.
- Integrate with Dedicated's billing/credits for burst usage and with Private deployment's KMS/audit logs.

Key concepts:
- Thermal headroom: estimated remaining safe operating envelope for a rack or pod before GPU downclocking or cooling alarms.
- Predictive thermal model: time-series predictor using recent GPU temps, fan speeds, ambient sensors, and workload intensity to forecast headroom over next 30–180 minutes.
- Burst credits: each tenant has a burst token bucket funded by reserved capacity + optional purchased burst credits. Credits are consumed when autoscaler permits above-reservation usage that increases thermal load.
- Soft-isolation lanes: when headroom is low, scheduler shifts tenants into lanes with stricter concurrency and smaller batch sizes to reduce heat generation while degrading throughput predictably.
- Thermal cooldown cooldown windows: enforced cooldown periods after detected thermal events; important to avoid oscillation.

Architecture (high level):
- Sensor input layer: GPU telemetry (temperature, power draw), chassis sensors (inlet temp), rack PDUs, and cluster-level HVAC indicators. In Private deployments, allow site integrators to map sensors.
- Thermal modeling microservice: lightweight predictor (moving window + small LSTM/ARIMA ensemble) deployed per site. Exposes headroom score [0..1].
- Autoscaler policy engine: extends existing autoscaler with thermal-aware policy hooks. Policy decisions consider target SLO, headroom, burst credit balance, and tenant priority.
- Scheduler adapter: enforces soft-isolation lanes, per-pod batch adjustments, and concurrency limits; can preempt opportunistic tasks.
- Console + telemetry: expose headroom, predicted thermal risk, and per-tenant burst credit consumption. Emit events to tracing and alerts.

Policy examples:
- Normal: headroom > 0.6 -> allow usual elastic burst up to burst credits.
- Caution: 0.35 < headroom <= 0.6 -> allow only short bursts (max 60s) with reduced batching; prefer routing to cooler racks/regions.
- Emergency: headroom <= 0.35 -> disable opportunistic bursts, enable strict lane isolation, throttle throughput to reservation level, send page to ops.

APIs / Config knobs:
- site.config.thermal_profile: enum {edge, colo, enterprise} with defaults and cooling latency estimates.
- tenancy.policy.burst_credit_budget: numeric tokens per-month.
- autoscaler.policy.thermal_thresholds: float list for caution/emergency.
- ops.runbook.cooldown_override: bool (manual eviction/cooldown window control).

SLOs and metrics:
- Customer-facing SLOs remain latency p50/p95 targets; thermal interventions should be reflected as events with reason codes.
- New internal metrics: headroom_score, predicted_time_to_throttle, per-tenant_burst_credit_balance, thermal_eviction_count, cooling_duration.

Operational playbook (brief):
- Alert types: headroom_warn, headroom_critical, unexpected_temp_spike.
- Runbook steps for headroom_warn: migrate low-priority tenants, reduce batch size, notify SEs. For critical: trigger emergency lanes, escalate to SRE and facilities, enable cooldown windows.
- Post-incident: generate incident report with thermal telemetry, model predictions vs reality, and recommended hardware ops.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (sandbox): deploy model in read-only mode in staging and a subset of non-production sites to validate predictions.
- Phase 1 (opt-in): allow select customers to opt into thermal-aware bursting (give burst credits at discount). Monitor behavior for 8 weeks.
- Phase 2 (default soft): enable for all on-prem pools with conservative thresholds and UI opt-outs.
- Phase 3 (tight): default to stricter policies and integrate with Dedicated billing and console explanations.

Safety, risks, and mitigations:
- Risk: model false positives causing unnecessary throttles -> mitigation: conservative thresholds, manual override, provide audit trail for customers.
- Risk: sensor unreliability across customer sites -> mitigation: fall back to simple heuristics (PDU power, observed GPU throttle events) and require site mapping.
- Risk: adversarial tenants gaming burst credits -> mitigation: anomaly detection on credit usage and rate-limits on credit top-ups.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Which predictive model performs best within 30–60s horizon vs 10–30min horizon? Data science experiment needed.
- How to surface thermal events in the Console without alarming customers unnecessarily? UX research needed.
- Cost model: how to price burst credits for on-prem Dedicated customers accounting for increased cooling costs?
- Integration points with facilities teams for HVAC telemetry ingestion.

Simulation notes and experiments:
- Initial simulator notebook reproduced heat soak on a 6U rack using workload traces from Dec 2024. Findings: short 90s spikes cause minimal headroom loss; sustained 20min 100% utilization creates >40% headroom drop.
- Attachments: simulation graphs, sample traces, and tradeoff matrix (linked above).

Appendix:
- Short glossary: headroom, burst credits, lane isolation, cooldown window.
- Contact: Priya Nair (product lead), Marco Ruiz (infra eng), Avery Chen (SRE).

Notes to self:
- Need to loop in Solutions Eng for enterprise site mapping template and add airbags for air-gapped sites.
- Add a small RFC for billing changes to account for burst credits consumed during thermal events.
